trust_decision.summary: The client-controlled If-None-Match / If-Match header value gets split with a backtracking regex /\s*,\s*/ inside the private helper etag_matches?. This happens with no bound on cost, so a long run of whitespace with no comma costs quadratic time.

landing_point.why: The summary names ETag header handling. Searching for ETag leads to the etag helper at lib/sinatra/base.rb:623 and then to its only regex, in etag_matches?.

fix_sites.entry_point: Public helper Sinatra::Helpers#etag (lib/sinatra/base.rb:623), called from any app route and fed by the HTTP If-None-Match / If-Match request headers
fix_sites.module_kind: core helper (same file as the request/response classes)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The Accept parsing regexes (lib/sinatra/base.rb:32-33) and the respond_with split (sinatra-contrib/lib/sinatra/respond_with.rb:115) parse other headers (content negotiation, not conditional GET), so a solver would rightly call them a neighbouring feature outside the ETag advisory.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A comma-separated ETag list with optional whitespace ("\"bar\", \"foo\"") must still match, and '*' must keep its new_resource semantics. A fix that drops the whitespace trimming or rejects long headers breaks the existing 304/412 behaviour.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The same idiom, split(/\s*;\s*/), runs on the negotiated mime type, which can come from the client's Accept header via preferred_type (lines 112-113).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already exists in the real code with the same \s*SEP\s* split idiom. A maintainer would write it naturally to strip parameters. Reachability depends on the Accept scan and on whether AcceptEntry#to_str keeps non-space whitespace (lib/sinatra/base.rb:106 deletes only ' ').

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Accept header scan with HEADER_PARAM / HEADER_VALUE_WITH_PARAMS (lib/sinatra/base.rb:32-33), where AcceptEntry re-scans HEADER_PARAM (lib/sinatra/base.rb:99).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is another header parser on untrusted input in the same Request class. A planted \s*,\s* split of Accept or Accept-Encoding here would read naturally, but it is a where-type sibling only.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace split(/\s*,\s*/) with split(',').map(&:strip), which is exactly the published fix and is found immediately.

out_of_scope_notes: The Accept header parsing regexes (lib/sinatra/base.rb:32-33, 99, 141) are applied to client input in a different feature and were not touched by this advisory.
rack-protection host_authorization splits Host on /:\d+\z/ (rack-protection/lib/rack/protection/host_authorization.rb:24,85). This is a different header and module and was not examined further.
unverified: The repo size was not measured (no shell). tiny_repo is inferred from sinatra being a small gem with a few-hundred-KB lib/, and repo_mb is left null.
Not checked: whether Ruby >= 3.2 regex memoization neutralises the quadratic split on modern Ruby. If it does, the hidden tests need Ruby < 3.2 or a timing threshold that holds there.
Not checked: whether the respond_with.rb:115 split is reachable with attacker-controlled whitespace after the Accept scan and AcceptEntry#to_str.
The second fix commit 8ff496bd is a merge commit (PR #1823) and the diff shows no content for it. It is assumed to add no other source change.
